design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (independent_living_billing_and_move_out) - Okafor household, Larkspur at Juniper Point.

[Step 0 - draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0034_senior_living_operator/independent_living_billing_and_move_out/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. independent_ext_final_month_charge takes 6, root independent_ext_closing_payment takes 5. Occupied by task 0: independent_ext_period_late_fee, independent_ext_annual_increase_fee, independent_ext_advance_payment and their tools (continuing residency: late fee, annual increase, advance payment). Claimed here, disjoint: the move-out side - the fee end date of a residency under notice and the settlement of an ending residency - with tools post_final_month_charge_713925f6 (agent) and make_closing_payment_d2bd6461 (user). After this task every extended policy is claimed; no headroom is reserved and nothing is left idle.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: the POA son wants to pay, in one payment he authorizes, everything the apartment will still cost until it is handed back (his father moved into Larkspur assisted living; notice signed 2026-10-20 with intended vacate 2026-11-09). Scored core: the closing amount (call 8, owner=user). Prerequisite (state form, value_input): the closing amount waits on the ledger carrying a monthly fee charge for the final month running from its first day through the date fees end -> the November base fee charge (agent, on_request, 6 factors). Depth: goal -> prerequisite sentence -> fee end date (notice period by the move the notice states, later of the intended vacate date) -> rate span -> courtesies -> closing amount. Breadth: 13 months of ledger, the recorded November increase, the assisted living residency (cross-difficulty: transfer tier and care level), payment standing and autopay history, amenity quantities, ledger balance.

[Base-invariant card] Final-month charge (subject independent_monthly_fee_charge): independent_monthly_billing.billing_on_live_residency - status notice_given is allowed; independent_fee_end_and_proration has no gate on this subject (policy_scope) and its rule fixes the fee end date: after a notice stating a move to Larkspur assisted living, the later of the vacate date (before surrender, the intended vacate date) and the notice date plus internal_transfer_notice_days (7 for a One-Bedroom). Overrides declared: base's transfer fee-end sentence (memory care moves add memory_transfer_notice_days 0) and base's proration by the actual days of the month is superseded by a 30-day basis for the final month, with the courtesies applied once. Closing payment (subject independent_payment): payment_on_open_account - notice_given allowed; certified_funds_restriction - no returned payment in 365 days, so a one-time ACH is accepted. Override declared: the closing payment's carpet cleaning share supersedes base 'The carpet_cleaning fee of the apartment type is charged once when the apartment is vacated' for internal transfers. No time gate applies to either subject (temporal_feasibility is empty).

[Business-object card] Residency 14a3bfcc-... (JP-208, One-Bedroom, single). Final month = the calendar month after the last month billed (October 2026, base fee 3968.00 through 2026-10-31). Rows read: the October full-month base fee charge (last day billed, fee billed), the 12 ACH autopay payments 2025-11..2026-10 (the 2025-10-14 move-in check falls just outside 12 months), no late fee, no returned payment, latest pet/storage/parking charges (quantity 1 each). The deposit receipt 2025-09-22 was applied in full at move-in (deposit held 0.00); the move-in check settled the prorated move-in fee, community fee, pet registration and first amenities net of the deposit credit; the ledger balance is 0.00 at the opening.

[Problem-tree card] root independent_ext_closing_payment (make_closing_payment_d2bd6461, owner user). Edge: -> independent_ext_final_month_charge, kind value_input, gate ledger_balance, form state, sentence 'The closing amount is worked out only after the ledger carries, wherever the residency's fees end after the last day already billed, a monthly fee charge for the final month running from its first day through the date the fees end.' (affirmative direction; task 0's charter also carries a negated-direction sentence), resolved by post_final_month_charge_713925f6 (agent). False at opening: the last base fee charge ends 2026-10-31 while fees run to 2026-11-09; balance 0.00. Only the final month policy's write books a charge for the final month (monthly billing on fee_due_day is not a task write and November has not come). Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a monthly fee charge on the ledger covering the final month through the fee end date); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly the final month through the fee end date, and only wherever the fees end after the last day already billed (round 2, F-2). Derivation: sentence + ledger (no November charge) + final month policy rule (it posts the final month's base fee charge) -> post the November charge first. Deletion sensitivity: skipping it leaves the ledger balance 0.00 and the closing amount 227.50 instead of 1375.76. user_scenario mentions no November charge; tools validate nothing.

[Factor card] Final-month charge (expected 1148.26; baseline_result 2513.07): notice_period parameter - the notice states a move to Larkspur assisted living -> internal_transfer_notice_days 7 -> 2026-10-27, so the fee end is the intended vacate date 2026-11-09; baseline move_out_notice_days 30 -> 2026-11-19 -> 2424.10. Tiers: memory care move -> memory_transfer_notice_days 0; assisted living move -> 7; any other notice -> 30; all three reachable under a standing notice (termination_reason resident_notice, transfer_assisted, transfer_memory). recorded_increase_span method - fee 4206.08 recorded effective 2026-11-01, the first day of the final month -> 1261.824 gross; baseline the October fee 3968.00 -> 1083.26. residence_courtesy parameter - 12 whole months since 2025-10-14 -> 1.0 (baseline 0 -> 1160.88). standing_courtesy parameter, multi-source (late fee count AND returned payment count in both tiers) - clean 12 months -> 2.0 (baseline -> 1173.50). autopay_courtesy parameter - 12/12 ACH autopay -> 1.0 (baseline -> 1160.88). care_transition_courtesy parameter, cross-difficulty assisted - Care Level 2 -> 5.0 (baseline -> 1211.35). The later-of-intended-vacate rule is part of the baseline (it applies to every customer under notice), not a factor. Near-misses: the 2025-10-14 move-in check would make the autopay tier partial if counted (it is 12 months and 14 days old, outside the window); the 3968.00 October fee is the fee billed but not the fee for November days. Closing amount (expected 1375.76; baseline_result 185.00): transfer_cleaning_share parameter, cross-difficulty assisted - the move-out carpet cleaning fee charged at vacate is 50 percent of 185.00 -> 92.50 (baseline 185.00 -> 1468.26); final_month_pets/storage/parking parameters - quantity 1 each -> 35.00/45.00/55.00 (baselines 1340.76/1330.76/1320.76); ledger_settlement method - balance 1148.26 owed -> added (baseline 227.50).

[World rows] customers: Raymond (name, DOB 1938-11-03, ssn 2317; representative Daniel, financial_poa). independent_residencies: notice_given residency (notice 2026-10-20, transfer_assisted, intended vacate 2026-11-09, fee 4206.08 effective 2026-11-01 recorded after the 2026-08-21 notice - the new-resident guarantee ended 2026-10-14; balance 0.00). assisted_residencies: active Care Level 2 residency since 2026-10-19 (admission_source larkspur_independent) - removing it moves the notice period to 30 days, the carpet share to 100 percent and the care courtesy to 0. independent_ledger: deposit, move-in month, 12 full months with amenities, all payments by autopay since November 2025. Automatic clauses checked: no late fee is due (every statement paid on the 1st), no increase is pending (recorded), no credit balance, the deposit is fully applied, the AL community fee is waived for internal transfers on the AL side; no obligation outside this task is lit.

[Persona] Daniel is calm and methodical, volunteers the move to assisted living, the notice, the 2026-11-09 hand-back and the wish to pay everything through the end in one payment he authorizes himself; identity only on request; agrees to postings the representative says are needed; authorizes exactly the amount given and closes. He never names a charge, a proration or a figure.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name, DOB) -> verify (DOB, ssn) -> read residency, ledger, assisted residency -> unlock/call post_final_month_charge_713925f6(residency, 2026-11-09, 1148.26) -> unlock_user; Daniel calls make_closing_payment_d2bd6461(residency, 1375.76).

[Verification run] check_compute -> '1.json 2 11 2 94 28 9 True ... COMPUTE OK' (recompute equals 1148.26 and 1375.76 and every declared baseline figure). check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_grounding, check_cross_fire all OK (round 2 re-run).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the closing payment prose, the final month prose, the tool schemas and the finder rows: the closing waits on a November charge (none on the ledger; fees end after the last billed day); the final month rule gives fee end 2026-11-09 (assisted living move: 2026-10-27, intended vacate later), 9 days at the recorded 4206.08 on a 30-day basis = 1261.82, less 9 percent courtesy = 1148.26; the closing rule gives 92.50 + 135.00 + 1148.26 = 1375.76. Same as gold; no second reading found.

[Round 2 rework - policy-task audit] F-2: the closing prerequisite sentence now reads 'The closing amount is worked out only after the ledger carries, wherever the residency's fees end after the last day already billed, a monthly fee charge for the final month running from its first day through the date the fees end.', at the strength of its condition. F-3: storage, parking and pet ladders now charge the fee once for each unit at two or more, matching base 'per unit'. F-5: the 'care residency is active' narrowing is removed from the fee end; the notice period follows only the move the notice states, and the deviation for memory care moves (0 days) is declared against base 'After a notice stating a move to a Larkspur assisted living or memory care residence ...'. F-6: the carpet override now fixes the fee charged when the apartment is vacated ('The move-out carpet cleaning fee charged when the apartment is vacated follows where the resident is moving, and the closing amount carries that same fee'), so the vacate charge and the closing share are one figure (92.50) and nothing is left owed. F-8: notice_period_end (unreachable nonpayment tier, mislabelled method) and surrender_floor (one reachable tier) are struck; the later-of-intended-vacate rule moved into the baseline; replaced by notice_period (parameter, three reachable tiers) and residence_courtesy (parameter). Re-run: final month 1160.88 -> 1148.26, closing 1388.38 -> 1375.76; factor_sensitivity, tracing, closure flips and business effects updated in the same pass.

[Round 3 rework - policy-task audit revision 2] N-2: the overwrite of base 'After a notice stating a move to a Larkspur assisted living or memory care residence, and for an internal transfer recorded without notice, the fee end date is the later of the vacate date and the notice date plus internal_transfer_notice_days calendar days.' is now replaced by a full sentence of the final month rule: 'For a notice stating a move to a Larkspur assisted living or memory care residence, and for an internal transfer to either recorded without notice, the fee end date is the later of the vacate date and the notice date plus the notice period that move carries.' - so the no-notice transfer branch and the vacate-date floor survive, and the merged base reading agrees with the final month charge (later of vacate and notice + period). N-1: the base move-out-notice sentence 'The notice period is move_out_notice_days for a resident leaving Larkspur and internal_transfer_notice_days when the notice states a move to a Larkspur assisted living or memory care residence' is now declared superseded by the notice-period ladder (memory care 0 days), with independent_move_out_notice added to base_policy_refs; its eligibility gates apply only to notice recording and withdrawal, so this write's base preconditions are unchanged. No value of this task changed (1148.26 / 1375.76).
user_scenario: You are Daniel Okafor, calling Larkspur's Resident and Family Services desk on a Wednesday morning about your father Raymond Okafor's independent living apartment, JP-208 at Larkspur at Juniper Point in Littleton. You hold your father's financial power of attorney and you are on file as his representative. You are calm and methodical, the kind of person who likes to close things out properly. Your father moved into the assisted living building at Juniper Point on October 19, and you signed his notice on the apartment the next day; the family is clearing it out and the notice says you will hand it back on November 9. You live out of state and fly home Friday, so today you want to pay, in one payment, everything the apartment will still cost through the end - whatever the community will bill for it until it is handed back - so there is nothing left hanging once you are gone. You do not know the figure and you expect the representative to work it out and tell you. You will authorize the payment yourself as a one-time bank draft from your father's checking account once the representative sets it up and hands it to you, and you will enter the bank details yourself. Only when asked which account this is do you give your father's full name, Raymond Okafor; only when asked to verify do you give his date of birth, 1938-11-03, and the last four digits of his Social Security number, 2317. If asked for phone numbers, his is 9725550128 and yours is 9725550163; you are not sure of his email address. If the representative tells you that something has to be put on the apartment account before the figure can be settled, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the payment, you authorize it for exactly that amount and read back the confirmation reference. Once you hear it went through, you thank them and end the call.
